reigns.note: Eponym whose friendly house received Hercules on the Lacinian shore — not a civic king. Myscelus later named the colony for the sacred bones buried by the Aesar's mouth. Not promoted as a character node.
Landed with Iberian herds on Lacinian shores, rested at Croton's house, and prophesied that the place would become a city of Croton's numerous race — hospitality and foundation oracle, not a reign.

Son of Argive Alemon, whom sleeping Hercules commanded to desert Argos and mark out walls where the hero had rested — Ovid's founder of Crotona. Pausanias instead frames Croton as a Lacedaemonian colony under Polydorus (3.3.1); both strands stand without a padded king-list.

King of Sparta under whom the Lacedaemonians sent colonies to Croton in Italy and to the Locri by the Western headland — colonial-era marker only, not a Crotoniate king. Not the Theban Polydorus son of Cadmus (`polydorus`). No named Spartan settler of Croton is attested in the seven lenses.
General of the Crotoniates when war arose with the Locri of Italy — wounded by Locrian Ajax, then first to sail to Achilles' White Island. Civic legend and hero-cult voyage, not a royal succession.
